title.value: AfriSenti: A Twitter Sentiment Analysis Benchmark for African Languages
title.justification: The title directly reflects the central theme of the paper, which is the creation and analysis of a sentiment analysis benchmark for African languages using Twitter data.
title.quote: In this paper, we introduce AfriSenti, a sentiment analysis benchmark that contains a total of >110,000 tweets in 14 African languages.

extractions.description: The paper introduces AfriSenti, a comprehensive Twitter sentiment analysis benchmark in 14 African languages, leveraging over 110,000 tweets. It addresses the underrepresentation of African languages in NLP research by providing a high-quality annotated dataset for sentiment analysis. The study outlines data collection, annotation processes, and challenges faced, especially in dealing with linguistic diversity and code-switching. Baseline experiments are conducted, highlighting the performance of various language models. AfriSenti aims to foster sentiment analysis research for African languages and invites further exploration and extension by the research community.

primary_category.justification: The paper focuses on sentiment analysis for African languages, which does not directly align with any predefined eco-responsible AI categories. It is primarily a language resource development effort.
primary_category.quote: Yet, there is little NLP research conducted on African languages. Crucial to enabling such research is the availability of high-quality annotated datasets.

secondary_categories.justification: No direct or indirect relation to eco-responsible AI categories. The primary goal is linguistic resource development rather than environmental or sustainability-oriented applications.
secondary_categories.quote: Africa is home to over 2,000 languages from more than six language families and has the highest linguistic diversity among all continents.

primary_sub_category.justification: The focus of the paper on sentiment analysis and language resources does not fall under any specific eco-responsible sub-category.
primary_sub_category.quote: To enable sentiment analysis research in African languages, we present AfriSenti, the largest sentiment analysis benchmark for under-represented African languages.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: Given the focus on linguistic and NLP tools, there are no secondary eco-responsible sub-categories applicable.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: The datasets were used in the first Afrocentric SemEval shared task SemEval 2023 Task 12: Sentiment analysis for African languages (AfriSenti-SemEval).

new_primary_category.justification: The core of the paper involves developing a linguistic benchmark for sentiment analysis across diverse African languages, which requires a new category focused on linguistic and cultural resource enrichment.
new_primary_category.quote: In this paper, we introduce AfriSenti, a sentiment analysis benchmark that contains a total of >110,000 tweets in 14 African languages.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The paper focuses on sentiment analysis specifically for African languages, which are often considered low-resource in NLP studies, hence a new sub-category is suggested to encapsulate this niche action area.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: We further report baseline experiments conducted on the different datasets and discuss their usefulness.
